misconceptions.description: Treating serrations like a motor muffler
misconceptions.trigger: learner explains quieter flight only through motor noise reduction
misconceptions.feedback: The key mechanism is aerodynamic. Serrations influence how flow separates and how vortices form near the blade edge, which changes sound generation.

misconceptions.description: Assuming more edge complexity always improves acoustics
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes extreme serration density without discussing drag or performance tradeoffs
misconceptions.feedback: Acoustic performance depends on spacing, scale, stiffness, and flow regime. Too much geometric complexity can introduce new aerodynamic penalties.

misconceptions.description: Copying owl appearance rather than fluid-dynamic function
misconceptions.trigger: learner focuses on visual similarity instead of vortex-control behavior
misconceptions.feedback: Biomimetic transfer should focus on how edge geometry changes turbulence and pressure fluctuations, not on literal visual resemblance to feathers.
